The Vision

Not a rental. A home base.

A single property in La Ventana that our family and closest friends own a piece of. This is meant to be a real, buildable plan — not a vacation timeshare. This page lays out the land, the site plan, the costs as they stand today, and a genuine ask for people who want to be part of building it.

Why La Ventana

Close, but still quiet.

A small, growing town on the Sea of Cortez in Baja California Sur — about an hour from Los Cabos International Airport, without the density and prices of Cabo itself.

Wind & Water

World-class kiteboarding

One of the best kiteboarding and windsurfing towns in North America, on the open Sea of Cortez.

Sea Life

Fishing, diving & whales

World-class sportfishing, snorkeling, and scuba on the reefs, and whale watching in season. Jacques Cousteau called the Sea of Cortez "the world's aquarium."

Location

An hour from Los Cabos

Close enough for an easy flight, far enough to avoid the density and prices of Cabo itself.

Community

Real, year-round life

A growing mix of long-time locals and expats — not a resort strip, an actual town to be part of.

Things To Do

More than the compound.

La Ventana and El Sargento are already a destination in their own right — the desert trails and open water right outside the property are part of the draw.

On Two Wheels

Mountain biking

Singletrack winding through cardón forest and exposed reef, right in the hills above La Ventana and El Sargento — beginner to advanced.

Wind & Water

Kiteboarding & windsurfing

Consistent thermal winds on the open Sea of Cortez, most of the year.

Sea Life

Sportfishing

Mahi-mahi, marlin, and dorado are all within reach of local charters out of La Ventana.

On Land

Horseback riding

Beach and desert rides with local outfitters, for a slower way to see the coastline.

On The Water

Boat tours & wildlife encounters

Baja Wild Encounters and other local outfitters run ocean safaris out of town — whale sharks, mobula rays, sea lions, and dolphins, depending on season.

Off The Beaten Path

Natural hot springs

Rock-pooled hot springs along the coast, a short drive from town.

The Dome Model

How domes lower the bar to join.

Instead of asking everyone to buy into the whole property, we sell small plots — each sized for one dome — so people can join at a much lower cost. A dome plot in the $30–40K range is a far easier yes than a six-figure land purchase.

03

Friends & family buy in

Each person covers their plot's share of land + a dome.

04

Compound grows together

More plots fill in over time — everyone shares the courts & common space.

Ownership & Legal

How we'd actually own it.

La Ventana sits inside Mexico's coastal "restricted zone," so non-Mexicans can't hold title directly. This is routine — thousands of foreigners own in Baja — but the structure has to be set up correctly. Before any money moves, a Mexican real-estate attorney and notario público review title, zoning, water rights, and the ownership structure.

Fideicomiso

Bank trust

  • A Mexican bank holds title in trust
  • Beneficiaries (us) have full rights to use, build, sell, and pass it on
  • The standard route for residential property

Mexican Corporation

Shares in a Mexican company

  • A Mexican company owns the land outright and we own shares
  • Often the better fit for a multi-owner project selling plots
  • Needs accounting and annual filings

Clean Title, Not Ejido

What we're screening for

  • Much rural Baja land is ejido (communal) and can't be sold normally
  • We only pursue parcels with clear private title
  • Confirmed by a notario público before any deposit
Build Phases

We build in three phases.

Each phase is funded and finished before the next starts — so nobody is on the hook for the whole vision on day one.

Phase 01

Secure the ground

Close on the land. Legal structure, survey, boundary, access road, well or water connection, power. Nothing gets built until this is done.

Phase 02

First homes

Main house(s) for the core group plus the first round of dome plots for founding participants. Shared kitchen or palapa as the gathering point.

Phase 03

Shared life

Tennis court, volleyball court, common areas. Remaining dome plots offered to the wider circle as people are ready.

Looking Further Ahead

Beyond the first phases.

Once the core compound is built, there's room to grow into something bigger — a place that supports itself and the people who work remotely from it.

A Gathering Place To Work

Brewery & co-working space

  • Modeled on Impact Hub Antigua — a coworking space and community hub built around a shared courtyard
  • Desks, meeting space, and reliable internet for anyone on the compound working remotely
  • A small on-site brewery attached, doubling as the social space for events and evenings together
Growing Our Own Food

Vertical farms

  • Modeled on Freight Farms' Greenery S — a hydroponic farm built inside a standard shipping container
  • Grows leafy greens, herbs, and vegetables year-round, regardless of the desert climate outside
  • One unit can produce 2–6 tons of food a year — enough to genuinely feed the compound, not just a garden's worth
